speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if your symptoms started suddenly or gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very telling. How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do you have any personal or family history of neuromuscular disorders like myasthenia gravis or Lambert-Eaton syndrome? REQUEST TEST: Antibodies for AChR and MuSK.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); MuSK_Antibodies: Not Detected (Not in data); NORMAL READINGS (for MuSK as it was not in the provided test data).

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is highly unusual for your symptoms, as Tuberculosis typically presents with fever, night sweats, and cough rather than fluctuating muscle weakness and double vision. To clarify the situation, does the double vision resolve completely when you close one eye, and do you experience any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing? REQUEST TEST: Thyroid function tests and Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Thyroid_Function_Tests: NORMAL READINGS; Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated Acetylcholine Receptor antibodies combined with fluctuating weakness and ocular symptoms confirms this diagnosis, making the previous suggestion of tuberculosis incorrect. I recommend immediate referral to a neurologist for potential immunotherapy and physical therapy.
